Example · People Development

SMPS20003U · Workshop for the teachers of Methods and Procedures in Clinical Drug Development

In this real course, students write a clinical-trial protocol from a medical case. This imagined People Development workshop helps the course's teachers mark the statistics in those protocols and judge how students use AI tools.

People DevelopmentUCPH SMPS20003UIllustrative levels and design
Service
People Development, tailored workshop (imagined for this example)
Participants
A hypothetical teaching team for the course
The course
MSc Pharmaceutical Sciences, 7.5 ECTS; students write a clinical-trial protocol
Format
Two half-days

Course description, kurser.ku.dk (external site)

Uses the Pharma Value Chain

Anchor

  • 10 Phase I / II / III Clinical development · anchored here
  • 11 Regulatory Clinical development · also touches

A protocol is designed for Phase I, II or III trials, and its analysis choices must hold up when a regulator reviews them.

  1. Pre-clinical
    1. 1Disease Understanding
    2. 2Target Identification
    3. 3Modality Selection
    4. 4Lead Identification
    5. 5Lead Optimisation & Candidate Selection
    6. 6Nonclinical Safety & DMPK
    7. 7Formulation & Drug Product Development (CMC)
  2. Clinical development
    1. 8Biomarker Development
    2. 9Clinical Pharmacology
    3. 10Phase I / II / III (anchored here)
    4. 11Regulatory (also touches)
  3. On-market
    1. 12Manufacturing
    2. 13Market Access (HEOR)
    3. 14Pharmacovigilance & Pharmacoepidemiology

Uses the PDS Competence Model

Assess and target Illustrative

  • Hypothesis testing

    Statistics · competency 6.3.4

    Start L2 · target L3

    Today, L2 Familiarity
    Run a basic test (t, χ², simple regression) on a pharma sample following an example.
    Target, L3 Proficiency
    Choose and interpret hypothesis tests honestly for real pharma questions (effect sizes, CIs, multiplicity).

    Why this target: We assume the teaching team can run a standard test. Judging a student's analysis plan also means choosing and interpreting tests for the trial in question, including multiplicity.

  • What can AI be used for? What can it not be used for?

    Use of AI in Education & Research · competency 5.3.1

    Start L1 · target L2

    Today, L1 Awareness
    Recognise the general capabilities and limits of current AI (LLMs and others) at a high level.
    Target, L2 Familiarity
    Place a candidate pharma use case on a "good fit / poor fit / unsafe" map following examples.

    Why this target: We assume the team has no shared way yet to decide which uses of AI in protocol writing are fine, which are poor and which are unsafe.

Uses the Pedagogic Practices

Deliver Illustrative

First half-day of two (120 minutes)

  1. 1Connections · 15 min
  2. 2Concepts · 20 min
  3. 3Concrete Practice · 45 min
  4. 4Concrete Practice · 25 min
  5. 5Conclusions · 15 min
  1. 1Connections15 min

    The section you dread marking

    Teachers stand at a wall and sort anonymised statistics sections from past reports into 'confident to mark' and 'unsure'.

    • Movement trumps sitting
    • Talking trumps listening
  2. 2Concepts20 min

    Three things every analysis plan must settle

    Short input on the estimand, multiplicity and sample size, with one annotated protocol page on screen.

    • Images trump words
    • Shorter trumps longer
  3. 3Concrete Practice45 min

    Rework your own case

    In pairs, teachers write the analysis section a strong student should produce for the case they set, then swap and review it against a checklist.

    • Writing trumps reading
    • Talking trumps listening
  4. 4Concrete Practice25 min

    AI: good fit, poor fit, unsafe

    Teachers place eight example uses of AI by students on a three-zone floor map and argue over the borderline cases.

    • Movement trumps sitting
    • Different trumps same
  5. 5Conclusions15 min

    One change before the next course run

    Each teacher writes one change to the protocol assignment, with a date, and reads it to the group.

    • Writing trumps reading
